🎙️ MikeCast

Daily Briefing — March 21, 2026

EXECUTIVE SUMMARY

Today's news highlights significant developments across various sectors. In the tech world, Elon Musk faces legal consequences for misleading investors during his acquisition of Twitter, while OpenAI is ambitiously working on a fully automated AI researcher. The business landscape is influenced by geopolitical tensions, with the US-Iran conflict impacting oil prices and market stability. In the corporate sphere, Uber's partnership with Rivian aims to revolutionize the robotaxi market, and the FTC scrutinizes Apple's news curation practices.

AI & TECH

Elon Musk has been found liable for misleading Twitter investors during his $44 billion acquisition of the platform, which he later renamed X. A jury determined that Musk misled investors by claiming there were too many bots on Twitter, a statement he used to try to back out of the deal. This legal decision underscores the challenges and responsibilities tech moguls face when making public statements that can significantly impact investor decisions. CNBC

OpenAI is embarking on an ambitious project to develop a fully automated AI researcher. This initiative aims to create an agent-based system capable of conducting research autonomously, potentially revolutionizing how scientific inquiries and technological advancements are pursued. This project reflects OpenAI's commitment to pushing the boundaries of AI capabilities and could have far-reaching implications for the tech industry and beyond. MIT Technology Review

Microsoft is rolling back some of its Copilot AI features on Windows, specifically reducing entry points in apps like Photos, Widgets, and Notepad. This decision comes as part of an effort to streamline user experience and address feedback regarding the AI's integration into the operating system. By refining its AI offerings, Microsoft aims to enhance user satisfaction and maintain its competitive edge in the tech market. TechCrunch

BUSINESS & MARKETS

The ongoing US-Iran conflict has led to a significant surge in New York heating oil prices, which have skyrocketed by 39% year-over-year. This increase is attributed to geopolitical tensions affecting global oil supply chains, highlighting the broader economic impact of international conflicts on domestic markets. Consumers and businesses alike are feeling the pressure as energy costs continue to rise. Times Herald-Record

President Donald Trump has stated that while he does not seek a ceasefire in the Iran conflict, he is considering "winding down" military operations. He emphasized the importance of other nations contributing to the policing of the Strait of Hormuz. This stance reflects ongoing strategic considerations and could influence future military and diplomatic engagements in the region. CNBC

The stock markets experienced volatility due to the Iran conflict, with the Dow and Nasdaq nearing correction territory before recovering slightly. The uncertainty surrounding geopolitical tensions has contributed to market instability, affecting investor confidence and leading to fluctuations in stock prices. CNBC

COMPANIES

Uber has announced a $1.25 billion deal with Rivian to develop a fleet of 50,000 robotaxis. This partnership aims to accelerate the deployment of autonomous vehicles, potentially transforming urban transportation and reducing reliance on human drivers. By investing heavily in this technology, Uber is positioning itself at the forefront of the autonomous vehicle market. Meyka

The FTC has issued a warning to Apple regarding its news curation practices, raising concerns about potential antitrust issues. The agency's scrutiny highlights the regulatory challenges tech giants face as they expand their influence over digital content and media distribution. This development could lead to increased regulatory oversight and impact Apple's business operations. MediaPost

Meta is facing a landmark social media addiction trial, with jury deliberations currently underway. The trial involves accusations against Meta and Google, focusing on the addictive nature of their platforms and the potential harm to users. The outcome could have significant implications for the tech industry, particularly regarding user safety and platform accountability. FOX 11 Los Angeles

NY SPORTS

The New York Yankees have optioned promising outfielder Jasson Dominguez to Triple-A, a strategic move likely aimed at further developing his skills before a potential major league call-up. This decision reflects the team's focus on nurturing young talent for future success. Sports Illustrated

In hockey, the New York team's offense struggled against the Capitals, leading to a disappointing performance. The team will need to regroup and address their offensive challenges in upcoming games to improve their standings. NHL.com

The Brooklyn Nets faced frustration after another defeat against the Knicks, extending their losing streak. This ongoing rivalry continues to be a source of tension and motivation for the Nets as they seek to break their losing pattern. New York Post

KEY TRENDS & INSIGHTS

  • Geopolitical tensions, particularly the US-Iran conflict, are significantly impacting energy prices and market stability. - Legal and regulatory scrutiny is intensifying for tech giants, with implications for business practices and market dynamics. - The push for autonomous vehicle technology is gaining momentum, with major investments from companies like Uber. - AI development continues to advance, with projects like OpenAI's automated researcher potentially reshaping research methodologies.

WHAT TO WATCH

  • Monitor the outcome of the social media addiction trial against Meta and Google for potential industry-wide impacts. - Keep an eye on developments in the US-Iran conflict, particularly any changes in military strategy or diplomatic negotiations. - Watch for further regulatory actions against Apple and other tech companies regarding content curation and antitrust concerns. - Follow the progress of Uber's partnership with Rivian as they work towards deploying a large-scale robotaxi fleet.

podcast_script:
[INTRO]

Hey there, welcome back to MikeCast! It’s March 21, 2026, and I’m your host, Mike, here to bring you the latest and greatest in news today. We’ve got a packed episode lined up for you, so grab your coffee and let’s dive right in. Today, we’re talking about some big moves in the tech world with OpenAI’s ambitious new project and Elon Musk’s latest courtroom drama. Plus, we’ll break down the latest in business and markets, including some eye-popping stock moves. And of course, we’ll catch up on the New York sports scene. So, let’s get started!

[AI & TECH SEGMENT]

Alright, let’s kick things off with the tech world, which is buzzing with some pretty fascinating developments. First up, OpenAI is making headlines again. They’re working on a project to build a fully automated AI researcher. This isn’t just any AI; it’s designed to operate independently, conducting research without human intervention. The goal here is to push the boundaries of what AI can achieve in terms of innovation and discovery. Why does this matter? Well, if successful, it could revolutionize how research is conducted across various fields, from medicine to environmental science, potentially speeding up breakthroughs that could benefit us all.

Now, speaking of AI, Microsoft is making some changes to its Copilot AI features on Windows. They’re scaling back the number of entry points for Copilot, starting with apps like Photos, Widgets, and Notepad. This decision seems to be a response to user feedback about the AI being a bit too intrusive. By reducing its presence, Microsoft is likely aiming to strike a better balance between helpful AI features and user control. It’s a reminder that even as AI advances, user experience remains a top priority.

Switching gears, let’s talk about Elon Musk. A jury has found that Musk misled investors during his acquisition of Twitter, which he later renamed X. Back in 2022, Musk had tweeted about Twitter having too many bots, which he claimed was a reason for trying to back out of the deal. The jury’s decision underscores the importance of transparency and honesty in business dealings, especially when it comes to high-stakes acquisitions like this one. It’s a significant ruling that could have implications for how other tech moguls handle similar situations in the future.

And lastly in tech, the Pentagon is set to adopt Palantir’s AI as a core system for the U.S. military. This move highlights the growing role of AI in national defense strategies. Palantir’s technology is known for its data analysis capabilities, which could enhance military operations by providing more accurate and timely information. It’s a big step in integrating advanced tech into military frameworks, potentially changing how operations are conducted.

[BUSINESS & MARKETS SEGMENT]

Now, let’s shift our focus to the business and markets scene. President Donald Trump has made waves by stating he doesn’t want a ceasefire in the ongoing conflict with Iran but is considering “winding down” military operations. This has had a ripple effect on the stock market. On Friday, stocks took a tumble due to the uncertainty surrounding the Iran conflict, with both the Dow and Nasdaq dipping into correction territory before recovering slightly. This volatility reflects the market’s sensitivity to geopolitical tensions and the potential economic impacts.

In a related development, the Dow Jones saw a late jump after the initial sell-off, as investors reacted to Trump’s comments about potentially winding down the conflict. It’s a reminder of how quickly markets can shift based on geopolitical news, and why it’s crucial for investors to stay informed about global events.

Meanwhile, heating oil prices in New York have skyrocketed, up 39% year-over-year. The ongoing U.S.-Iran conflict is a significant factor here, as it affects oil supply and prices. For New Yorkers, this means higher heating costs, which could impact household budgets, especially as we move through the tail end of winter.

[COMPANIES SEGMENT]

Alright, let’s dive into the latest from the corporate world. Uber is making a big bet on the future of transportation with a $1.25 billion deal with Rivian to develop a fleet of 50,000 robotaxis. This partnership is part of Uber’s strategy to expand its autonomous vehicle offerings, which could revolutionize urban transportation by reducing the need for human drivers and potentially lowering costs for consumers. It’s a bold move that underscores the growing interest in and potential of autonomous vehicles.

Meanwhile, the FTC is turning its attention to Apple, with the chair warning the company over its news curation practices. This comes amid broader scrutiny of tech giants and their influence over information dissemination. The FTC’s warning suggests there could be regulatory changes on the horizon aimed at ensuring fair and unbiased access to news content.

In other news, Meta is shutting down a project that CEO Mark Zuckerberg once called “the next frontier” for the company. Although the article doesn’t specify what the project was, this decision marks a significant shift in Meta’s strategy as they reassess their priorities and focus on more promising ventures.

Finally, a judge has rejected a preemptive fee bid by lawyers in a Google ad tech class action. This ruling is part of a broader legal battle over Google’s advertising practices, which have been under scrutiny for anti-competitive behavior. The decision could impact how legal fees are handled in similar cases moving forward, potentially affecting the dynamics of class action lawsuits against big tech companies.

[NY SPORTS SEGMENT]

Alright, sports fans, let’s catch up on the latest from the New York sports scene. The Yankees have made a roster move, optioning promising outfielder Jasson Dominguez to Triple-A. This decision is likely part of their strategy to give Dominguez more playing time and development opportunities before potentially bringing him back to the majors.

In hockey, the offense dried up for the New York team against the Capitals, marking a tough game for the squad. They’ll be looking to bounce back in their next matchup.

And over in basketball, the Nets are feeling the frustration after failing once again to break their losing streak against the Knicks. It was a hard-fought game, and the emotions were running high, as evidenced by the post-game comments. The rivalry between these two teams continues to be intense, and fans are eagerly anticipating their next showdown.

[MIKE'S PICKS SEGMENT]

Alright, it’s time for Big Mike’s hand-picked reads. If you’re looking for something intriguing to dive into, check out the piece on OpenAI’s ambitious project to create a fully automated researcher. It’s a fascinating look at where AI is headed and what it could mean for the future of innovation. Also, the story about Elon Musk’s legal troubles over the Twitter acquisition is a must-read for anyone interested in the intersection of tech and law. These stories offer a deep dive into the challenges and opportunities facing the tech industry today.

[OUTRO]

And that’s a wrap for today’s episode of MikeCast! Thanks for tuning in and catching up with us. If you enjoyed the show, be sure to subscribe and leave us a review. I’m Mike, signing off — until next time, stay curious and keep exploring!
